From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Appendix:Variations of "marina"

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
marina
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin marinus (“of the sea, marine”), by way of Italian marina and Spanish marina.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /məˈɹinə/
  • Hyphenation: ma‧ri‧na
  • Rhymes: -iːnə
    • Audio (Southern England):(file)

Noun

[edit]

marina (plural marinas)

  1. A harbour for small boats.
    It's a peaceful marina with not too many boats and yachts.
    • 2007 January 7, Alex Mindlin, “For a Shuttered Marina, Some Regret, Some Relief”, in The New York Times‎[1], archived from the original on 11 April 2021:
      The marina was a mainstay of the neighborhood, and Mr. O’Rourke was known for staging salsa and merengue concerts.

Related terms

[edit]
  • marine
  • Marines

Translations

[edit]
harbour
  • Bulgarian: яхт-клуб m (jaht-klub)
  • Dutch: jachthaven (nl), passantenhaven m or f (short-stay), watersporthaven m or f, plezierhaven m or f
  • Finnish: venesatama
  • French: port de plaisance (fr) m, marina (fr) f
  • German: Jachthafen (de) m, Bootshafen (de) m; (specialist, not generally understood also) Marina (de) f, Wasserwanderrastplatz m (short-stay)
  • Greek: μαρίνα (el) f (marína), λιμανάκι (el) n (limanáki)
  • Hebrew: מַעֲגָנָה (he) f (ma'aganá)
  • Italian: porticciolo (it) m, marina (it) f, porticciolo turistico, darsena (it) f
  • Lithuanian: prieplauka f
  • Manx: stashoon birling m
  • Norwegian:
    Bokmål: marina m, båthavn m or f, båthamn m or f
    Nynorsk: marina m, båthamn f
  • Polish: marina (pl) f
  • Portuguese: marina (pt) f
  • Russian: прича́л (ru) m (pričál)
  • Serbo-Croatian:
    Cyrillic: мари́на f
    Latin: marína (sh) f
  • Spanish: puerto deportivo m
  • Swedish: marina (sv), småbåtshamn (sv) c
  • Yiddish: יאַכטבאַסיין m (yakhtbaseyn)

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Feminine of marí (“marine”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [məˈɾi.nə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [maˈɾi.na]
  • Audio (Valencia):(file)
  • Hyphenation: ma‧ri‧na

Noun

[edit]

marina f (plural marines)

  1. female equivalent of marí (“sailor”)
  2. coast
  3. seascape
  4. navy
  5. marina

Adjective

[edit]

marina

  1. feminine singular of marí
